strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Loop
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce stages with intervening local bidiagonal coupling and uncoupling transformations on the full W*S vector. Each stage does one all-reduce dispatch followed by local element-wise operations (forward coupling, backward uncoupling). Total 8 all-reduce dispatches with maximum simplicity but no overlap or fusion.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather to enable per-rank shard ownership and localize coupling operations to boundary exchanges. After reduce-scatter, only neighboring shard boundaries need communication for bidiagonal coupling (point-to-point or small collectives), then all-gather reconstructs full vector. Increases dispatch count (16-24 collectives) but reduces per-stage payload and enables potential pipelining.

strategies.name: Fused Coupling Within All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-apply the bidiagonal coupling transformation before each all-reduce so the collective directly sums the coupled vectors, then post-process with uncoupling only once at the end. Requires carefully tracking which coupling state each rank holds during summation. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but changes local computation pattern to front-load coupling operations and batch uncoupling.

strategies.name: Ring-Based Iterative Bidiagonal Exchange
strategies.desc: Implements a custom ring algorithm where each rank sends its right boundary to rank+1 and receives from rank-1, accumulating bidiagonal contributions incrementally across W steps per stage. Replaces all-reduce with W point-to-point send/recv pairs per stage (if supported) or W small all-reduces on boundary slices. Trades few large collectives for many small boundary-only communications (8*W dispatches on S-sized boundaries).

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc:
Exploits the multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce (across devices within each node) followed by inter-node all-reduce on aggregated results, then broadcast back. For 224 ranks, structure as node-local reductions followed by cross-node leader communication. Doubles dispatch count (16 collectives: 8 intra-node + 8 inter-node) but reduces cross-node bandwidth by factor of devices-per-node and may leverage faster intra-node interconnect.
